note: Inhaled long-acting muscarinic (M3) antagonists (tiotropium, aclidinium, glycopyrronium, umeclidinium, revefenacin) are given to COPD patients without any biomarker; the class was built on human-receptor kinetics in CHO cells and cholinergic bronchospasm in dogs and guinea pigs.
label: COPD (antimuscarinics)

engagement.model: Human M1-M3 receptors in CHO cells; guinea-pig trachea; dog acetylcholine bronchospasm
engagement.note: Tiotropium left human M3 with a 34.7 h half-life (ipratropium 0.26 h) and protected dogs against acetylcholine bronchospasm longer than ipratropium.
engagement.short: Slow M3 off-rate, long dog bronchoprotection
engagement.quote: Ba 679 represents a novel type of antimuscarinic bronchodilator with a long duration of action, most likely due to its slow dissociation from Hm3-receptors.

engagement.model: Human M1-M3 receptors in CHO cells; guinea-pig trachea; dog acetylcholine bronchospasm
engagement.note: In 35 COPD patients single inhaled doses gave bronchodilation lasting 32 h, the sustained airway M3 blockade the off-rate predicted.
engagement.quote: The bronchodilator response was almost immediate; peak improvement in FEV1 was reached 1-4 h after test drug inhalation, and the duration of action extended to 32 h after the 20, 40 and 80 micrograms doses.
engagement.confidence: medium: abstract-level; DOI registered at doi.org (resolves to the ERS lookup for this DOI) but the publisher page returned 403, so the landing page itself was not read
engagement.reason: Sustained bronchodilation matched slow M3 off-rate
engagement.judgement: No receptor-occupancy measurement exists in patients; reversal of cholinergic tone (FEV1) is taken as the same-receptor read-out, as sweat chloride is for CFTR. Maesen's 1993 pilot (Eur Respir J 6:1031, no DOI in PubMed) already juxtaposed the preclinical duration claim with 6 patients but reported only 10-15 h, so the 1995 RCT is used.

dose.model: hM3 dissociation kinetics (CHO cells) and dog acetylcholine-bronchospasm duration
dose.note: The model set a dosing-interval target (once-daily occupancy from the slow M3 off-rate), not a human dose; no inhaled dose was derived from it.
dose.short: Kinetics set a once-daily interval, no dose
dose.quote: Ba 679 demonstrated a significantly longer duration of protection than an equipotent dose of ipratropium.

dose.model: hM3 dissociation kinetics (CHO cells) and dog acetylcholine-bronchospasm duration
dose.note: Once-daily interval held: 20-80 ug kept FEV1 up for 32 h with a dose-response; the dose itself came from clinical ranging 10-80 ug.
dose.short: Once-daily interval held; dose found empirically
dose.quote: A clear dose-response relationship was seen for peak FEV1 and for the average FEV1 over differing time periods during the 32 h observation period, 80 micrograms of test drug being superior to the 10 micrograms dose.
dose.confidence: medium: abstract-level; DOI registered at doi.org (resolves to the ERS lookup for this DOI) but the publisher page returned 403, so the landing page itself was not read
dose.judgement: Scored on the interval only. Two later strains were not scored as contra: (1) Casarosa 2009 (doi 10.1124/jpet.109.152470) found glycopyrrolate gave 0% dog bronchoprotection at 24 h at equieffective doses, and Sykes 2012 (doi 10.1124/jpet.112.194456) found physiological off-rates of 11 min (glycopyrronium) and 46 min (tiotropium) that cannot explain either drug's 24 h clinical duration; but the clinical 50 ug dose is not the dog's equieffective dose and neither source calls it a missed prediction. (2) Gavalda 2009 (doi 10.1124/jpet.109.151639) gave aclidinium a 29 h guinea-pig offset half-life supporting the once-daily 200 ug used in ACCLAIM (Jones 2011, doi 10.1186/1465-9921-12-55; trough FEV1 +59 to +67 mL) before development moved to 400 ug twice daily; no verified source states that comparison, so it is a note, not a status.

efficacy.model: Dog acetylcholine-induced bronchospasm; guinea-pig tracheal rings
efficacy.note: The model reads reversal of cholinergic bronchoconstriction, the reversible part of COPD airflow limitation; it is silent on inflammation and decline.
efficacy.quote: The duration of action in vivo was determined by means of acetylcholine-induced bronchospasms in dogs following inhalation of the drugs.

efficacy.model: Dog acetylcholine-induced bronchospasm; guinea-pig tracheal rings
efficacy.note: COPD airflow improved as the bronchospasm model said: peak FEV1 rose 20-25% of baseline versus 11% on placebo after carry-over correction.
efficacy.quote: Compared to placebo, tiotropium bromide produced significant improvements in FEV1, FVC, peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) and forced mid-expiratory flow (FEF25-75%).
efficacy.confidence: medium: abstract-level; DOI registered at doi.org (resolves to the ERS lookup for this DOI) but the publisher page returned 403, so the landing page itself was not read
efficacy.reason: Airflow improved as bronchospasm model said
efficacy.judgement: UPLIFT (Tashkin 2008, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa0805800) found tiotropium did not slow FEV1 decline over 4 years; not scored as contra because the pivotal models never predicted disease modification. The LPS guinea-pig remodelling model (Pera 2011, doi 10.1183/09031936.00146610) and the smoke-mouse anti-inflammatory model (Wollin 2010, doi 10.1016/j.pupt.2010.03.008) post-date UPLIFT and have no published patient comparison, so they do not open a new status.

safety.model: hM2 versus hM3 dissociation kinetics (CHO cells); dog pharmacology
safety.note: Faster dissociation from M2 than M3 was the rationale for sparing cardiac M2 receptors; dogs gave plasma levels, no patient comparison existed.
safety.quote: In addition, the drug showed "kinetic receptor subtype selectivity" by having a more rapid dissociation from Hm2 than from Hm1 and Hm3 receptors.

safety.model: Anaesthetised-dog heart-rate pharmacology with M2-sparing kinetics
safety.note: Dogs predicted a favourable cardiovascular profile for aclidinium (Gavalda 2009); in 3,630 high-risk COPD patients MACE was noninferior to placebo over 3 years.
safety.short: MACE noninferior to placebo in 3,630 patients
safety.quote: Among patients with COPD and increased cardiovascular risk, aclidinium was noninferior to placebo for risk of MACE over 3 years.
safety.confidence: high: abstract-level; model side is Gavalda 2009 (doi 10.1124/jpet.109.151639) which dosed aclidinium in dogs
safety.reason: No cardiac harm, as dog model said
safety.judgement: The dog heart-rate model is first found with the product in Gavalda 2009, so model_first_use_year is 2009 for this entry while the cell opens in 1993 on the M2-sparing rationale. The 2008 JAMA meta-analysis cardiovascular signal and the Respimat mortality question (TIOSPIR 2013) were not used: a meta-analysis is not a primary comparison under rule 1 and TIOSPIR compared devices of the same drug. Registry results-posted date for NCT01966107 was not looked up.
